subject: maths
title: Place Value to 10 000 and Beyond: Read, Write, Partition and Order Numbers
seo_title: Year 3 Place Value Worksheets: Numbers to 10 000 and Beyond, Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Recognise, represent and order natural numbers using naming and writing conventions for numerals beyond 10 000
meta_desc: Free Year 3 place value maths worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: the value of each digit with MAB and place value charts, numbers beyond 10 000 in words and numerals, standard and non-standard partitioning, and comparing and ordering. 100 NAPLAN-style questions with an answer key.
key_big: The place of a digit decides its value. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.
key_sub: The 5 in 45 307 is worth 5000. Write 0 for an empty place: four thousand and six is 4006. Count the digits before you compare: 10 200 is greater than 9870.
body_html:
Each place is worth 10 times more

Every digit sits in a place: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands or ten thousands. The place tells you what the digit is worth. 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, 10 hundreds make 1 thousand and 10 thousands make 10 000.

Reading and writing numbers

Say the thousands first, then the rest. Write 4-digit numbers with no space (4536). Put a small space in numbers with 5 or more digits (10 000, 45 307).

NumeralWords
4006four thousand and six
3020three thousand and twenty
10 000ten thousand
12 305twelve thousand, three hundred and five
Write in numerals

Write “four thousand and six” in numerals.

4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones. Write 4, 0, 0, 6.

Answer: 4006 (not 46, 406 or 40 006)

Partition in different ways

The standard way uses the value of each digit. A non-standard way regroups the places.

Partition

Partition 3462 in two ways.

Standard: 3000 + 400 + 60 + 2. Non-standard: 34 hundreds = 3400, so 3462 = 34 hundreds and 62 ones.

Answer: 3000 + 400 + 60 + 2 = 34 hundreds and 62 ones

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 5-digit number is greater than any 4-digit number. If both have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left.

Compare

23 504 ☐ 23 540

Ten thousands: 2 = 2. Thousands: 3 = 3. Hundreds: 5 = 5. Tens: 0 < 4.

Answer: 23 504 < 23 540

< means “is less than”. > means “is greater than”. The open side faces the bigger number.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out zeros (four thousand and six = 46 or 406)Write 0 for each empty place: 4006
Writing each part you hear (four thousand and six = 40 006)A thousands number has 4 digits: 4006
Giving the digit, not its value (the 5 in 45 307 is 5)The 5 is in the thousands place: 5000
Comparing the first digits only (9870 > 10 200)Count the digits first: 10 200 > 9870
Reading 10 000 as 100010 000 has 5 digits: ten thousand

faq.q: What place value does a Year 3 student learn in Australia?
faq.a: The Australian Curriculum (AC9M3N01) asks Year 3 students to recognise, represent and order numbers beyond 10 000. They name the value of each digit, read and write numbers in words and numerals, partition numbers in different ways and compare and order them.

MAB (multi-base arithmetic blocks) are the base-ten blocks used in Australian classrooms: a mini is 1, a long is 10, a flat is 100 and a big cube is 1000. Children build numbers with them to see what each digit is worth.

faq.q: How do you write 10 000 in Australia?
faq.a: Numbers with 5 or more digits are written with a small space between groups of three digits, such as 10 000 and 45 307. Four-digit numbers like 4536 are written with no space, and commas are not used.

faq.q: Is place value tested in NAPLAN?
faq.a: Yes. The Year 3 NAPLAN numeracy test often asks students to read, write, partition and order numbers, so regular practice with place value helps them answer these questions quickly and accurately.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 4 thousands = 4000. The digit is 4, but its value is 4000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 7409?

items.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 24 617?

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 58 371?

items.q: In 47 285, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: 47 285 has 4 ten thousands, 7 thousands, 2 hundreds, 8 tens, 5 ones. The thousands digit is 7.

items.q: In 63 914, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: 63 914 has 6 ten thousands, 3 thousands, 9 hundreds, 1 ten, 4 ones. The ten thousands digit is 6.

items.q: In 28 571, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 28 571 has 2 ten thousands, 8 thousands, 5 hundreds, 7 tens, 1 one. The hundreds digit is 5.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the hundreds place?
items.e: In 3681 the 6 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 6 hundreds = 600.

items.q: Which number has a 4 in the thousands place?
items.e: In 4729 the 4 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 4 thousands = 4000.

items.q: Which number has an 8 in the ten thousands place?
items.e: In 81 532 the 8 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 8 ten thousands = 80 000.

sets.title: Read and write numbers in words and numerals

items.q: Write “four thousand and six” in numerals.
items.e: Four thousand and six is 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones: 4006. Write 0 for the empty hundreds and tens places.

items.q: Write “three thousand and twenty” in numerals.
items.e: Three thousand and twenty is 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens, 0 ones: 3020. Write 0 for the empty hundreds and ones places.

items.q: Write “seven thousand, four hundred and eight” in numerals.
items.e: Seven thousand, four hundred and eight is 7 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 8 ones: 7408. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: Write “eight thousand and eleven” in numerals.
items.e: Eight thousand and eleven is 8 thousands, 0 hundreds, 1 ten, 1 one: 8011. Write 0 for the empty hundreds place.

items.q: Write “five thousand and ninety” in numerals.
items.e: Five thousand and ninety is 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 9 tens, 0 ones: 5090. Write 0 for the empty hundreds and ones places.

items.q: How do you write 2604 in words?
c: two thousand, six hundred and four
two thousand, six hundred and forty
items.e: 2604 has 2 thousands, 6 hundreds, 4 ones. Say it: two thousand, six hundred and four.

items.q: How do you write 9017 in words?
items.e: 9017 has 9 thousands, 1 ten, 7 ones. Say it: nine thousand and seventeen. 17 is seventeen, not seventy.

items.q: How do you write 4500 in words?
items.e: 4500 has 4 thousands, 5 hundreds. Say it: four thousand, five hundred.

items.q: Which number is ten thousand?
items.e: Ten thousand is 10 thousands. It has 5 digits: 1 and four zeros, written 10 000. 1000 is only one thousand.

items.q: How many thousands make 10 000?
items.e: 10 000 is 1 ten thousand, and 1 ten thousand = 10 thousands. Count in thousands: 1000, 2000, … 9000, 10 000. That is 10 thousands.

items.q: Write “twelve thousand, three hundred and five” in numerals.
items.e: Twelve thousand, three hundred and five is 1 ten thousand, 2 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones: 12 305. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: Write “twenty thousand and forty” in numerals.
items.e: Twenty thousand and forty is 2 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens, 0 ones: 20 040. Write 0 for the empty thousands, hundreds and ones places.

items.q: Write “sixteen thousand and seven” in numerals.
items.e: Sixteen thousand and seven is 1 ten thousand, 6 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 7 ones: 16 007. Write 0 for the empty hundreds and tens places.

items.q: Write “thirty thousand, five hundred” in numerals.
items.e: Thirty thousand, five hundred is 3 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 5 hundreds, 0 tens, 0 ones: 30 500. Write 0 for the empty thousands, tens and ones places.

items.q: Write “twenty-five thousand and fifty” in numerals.
items.e: Twenty-five thousand and fifty is 2 ten thousands, 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens, 0 ones: 25 050. Write 0 for the empty hundreds and ones places.

items.q: How do you write 15 080 in words?
c: ten thousand, five hundred and eighty
one thousand, five hundred and eighty
items.e: 15 080 has 1 ten thousand, 5 thousands, 8 tens. Say it: fifteen thousand and eighty.

items.q: How do you write 40 300 in words?
items.e: 40 300 has 4 ten thousands, 3 hundreds. Say it: forty thousand, three hundred.

items.q: How do you write 11 011 in words?
c: eleven thousand, one hundred and one
eleven thousand, one hundred and ten
one thousand, one hundred and eleven
items.e: 11 011 has 1 ten thousand, 1 thousand, 1 ten, 1 one. Say it: eleven thousand and eleven.

items.q: Write “forty thousand” in numerals.
items.e: Forty thousand is 4 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones: 40 000. 4000 is only four thousand.

items.q: Write “nineteen thousand” in numerals.
items.e: Nineteen thousand is 1 ten thousand and 9 thousands, then 0 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones: 19 000. 1900 is one thousand, nine hundred.

sets.title: Partition numbers in standard and non-standard ways

items.q: What number is 6000 + 200 + 40 + 3?
items.e: 6000 + 200 + 40 + 3 = 6243. Each part gives one digit.

items.q: What number is 5000 + 60 + 3?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 5000 + 60 + 3 = 5063.

items.q: What number is 9000 + 700 + 8?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 9000 + 700 + 8 = 9708.

items.q: What number is 20 000 + 4000 + 7?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 20 000 + 4000 + 7 = 24 007.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 80 000 + 1000 + 400 + 50 = 81 450.

items.q: Which shows 3462 partitioned into place values?
items.e: Write the value of each digit: 3000 + 400 + 60 + 2.

items.q: Which shows 4085 partitioned into place values?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 4000 + 80 + 5. A zero adds nothing, so it does not get its own part.

items.q: Which shows 30 619 partitioned into place values?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 30 000 + 600 + 10 + 9. A zero adds nothing, so it does not get its own part.

items.q: Which shows 52 070 partitioned into place values?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 50 000 + 2000 + 70. A zero adds nothing, so it does not get its own part.

items.q: 7000 + ☐ + 50 + 4 = 7354. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 7354 has 3 in the hundreds place. 3 hundreds = 300, so the missing part is 300.

items.q: 40 000 + 6000 + ☐ + 8 = 46 028. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 46 028 has 2 in the tens place. 2 tens = 20, so the missing part is 20.

items.q: ☐ + 2000 + 900 + 1 = 32 901. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 32 901 has 3 in the ten thousands place. 3 ten thousands = 30 000, so the missing part is 30 000.

items.q: How many hundreds are there in 3462 altogether?
items.e: Cover the digits to the right of the hundreds place: 3462 → 34. So 3462 has 34 hundreds altogether: 34 hundreds = 3400, with 62 left over. The hundreds digit is only 4.

items.q: How many tens are there in 4570 altogether?
items.e: Cover the digits to the right of the tens place: 4570 → 457. So 4570 has 457 tens altogether: 457 tens = 4570. The tens digit is only 7.

items.q: How many thousands are there in 26 300 altogether?
items.e: Cover the digits to the right of the thousands place: 26 300 → 26. So 26 300 has 26 thousands altogether: 26 thousands = 26 000, with 300 left over. The thousands digit is only 6.

items.q: How many hundreds are there in 12 800 altogether?
items.e: Cover the digits to the right of the hundreds place: 12 800 → 128. So 12 800 has 128 hundreds altogether: 128 hundreds = 12 800. The hundreds digit is only 8.

items.q: 3462 = 34 hundreds and ☐ ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 34 hundreds = 3400. 3462 − 3400 = 62. So 3462 = 34 hundreds and 62 ones.

items.q: 5306 = 4000 + ☐ + 6. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 5306 is 5000 + 300 + 6. Here only 4000 is used, so 1000 moves to the hundreds part: 1000 + 300 = 1300. Check: 4000 + 1300 + 6 = 5306.

items.q: Which is another way to make 2750?
items.e: 27 hundreds = 2700 and 5 tens = 50. 2700 + 50 = 2750. (50 tens is 500, and 275 hundreds is 27 500.)

items.q: Which is not equal to 4800?
items.e: 4 thousands and 8 tens = 4000 + 80 = 4080, not 4800. 48 hundreds = 4800, 4000 + 800 = 4800 and 480 tens = 4800.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 2 tens. So 4352 > 4325.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 10 200 has 5 digits and 9870 has only 4, so 10 200 is greater. Do not just look at the first digit: count the digits first.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 4 tens is more than 0 tens. So 23 540 > 23 504.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 9 tens is more than 8 tens. So 6098 > 6089.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 12 001 has 5 digits and 9999 has only 4, so 12 001 is greater. Do not just look at the first digit: count the digits first.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 10 000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 1000. The arrow is 2 marks after 5000: 5000, 6000, 7000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each mark is 1000. The arrow is 1 mark after 25 000: 25 000 + 1000 = 26 000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 4000 to 5000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100, not 10. The arrow is 3 marks after 4000: 4000 + 300 = 4300.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 6 hundreds is more than 5 hundreds. So 7605 > 7560. 7605 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 9899 and 9989 have only 4 digits, so they are smaller. Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 1 ten is more than 0 tens. So 10 010 > 10 001. 10 010 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 1 ten is more than 0 tens. So 35 210 > 35 201. 35 210 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 8 tens is more than 7 tens. So 4087 > 4078. 4078 is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: 9870 is the only number with 4 digits, so it is the smallest, even though 9 is a big digit.

items.q: Which number is between 6400 and 6500?
items.e: Numbers between 6400 and 6500 have 6 thousands and 4 hundreds. 6450 has 6 thousands, 4 hundreds and 5 tens. 6045 has 0 hundreds, and 6540 has 5 hundreds.

items.q: Which number is between 19 000 and 20 000?
items.e: Numbers between 19 000 and 20 000 start with 19 thousand. 19 500 is 19 thousands and 5 hundreds. 1950 has only 4 digits, so it is much smaller.

items.q: Put 5260, 5026, 5602 in order from smallest to largest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 5026 < 5260 (hundreds: 0 < 2). 5260 < 5602 (hundreds: 2 < 6). So the order is 5026, 5260, 5602.

items.q: Put 12 450, 9980, 12 405 in order from smallest to largest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 9980 < 12 405 (fewer digits). 12 405 < 12 450 (tens: 0 < 5). So the order is 9980, 12 405, 12 450.

items.q: Put 30 060, 30 600, 3600 in order from smallest to largest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 3600 < 30 060 (fewer digits). 30 060 < 30 600 (hundreds: 0 < 6). So the order is 3600, 30 060, 30 600.

items.q: Put 8150, 8510, 8015 in order from largest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 8015 < 8150 (hundreds: 0 < 1). 8150 < 8510 (hundreds: 1 < 5). So the order is 8510, 8150, 8015.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: Each mark is 1000. The arrow is halfway between 3000 and 4000, so it shows about 3500.

items.q: At the footy, 45 307 people watched the game. What is the value of the digit 5 in 45 307?
items.e: The 5 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 5 thousands = 5000.

items.q: The school library has 4060 books. Which shows 4060 partitioned?
items.e: 4060 has 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones: 4000 + 60.

items.q: Mum’s car has travelled 23 406 km. Which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: 23 406 has 2 ten thousands, 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones. The thousands digit is 3.

items.q: Four friends counted their steps on a school excursion. Chloe: 8350; Matilda: 8503; Cooper: 8035; Amelia: 8530. Who walked the most steps?
items.e: All four numbers have 8 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 8503 and 8530 have 5 hundreds. Then the tens: 3 tens > 0 tens, so 8530 is the greatest. Amelia walked the most.

items.q: The crowds at four footy games were 32 410, 32 140, 31 999, 32 401. Which crowd was the smallest?
items.e: All four have 3 ten thousands. Compare the thousands: 31 999 has only 1 thousand, the others have 2. So 31 999 is the smallest.

items.q: Raffle tickets come in books of 100. How many books make 3400 tickets?
items.e: 3400 = 34 hundreds, because 34 × 100 = 3400. So there are 34 books.

items.q: Pencils come in boxes of 10. The school buys 2350 pencils. How many boxes is that?
items.e: 2350 = 235 tens, because 235 × 10 = 2350. So there are 235 boxes.

items.q: Isla writes “ten thousand, four hundred” in numerals. What should she write?
items.e: Ten thousand, four hundred is 1 ten thousand, 0 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones: 10 400.

items.q: A sign says a country town has a population of “seventeen thousand and forty”. What is this in numerals?
items.e: 1 ten thousand, 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens and 0 ones: 17 040.

items.q: A truck driver drove 12 450 km in March. How do you write 12 450 in words?
c: twelve thousand, four hundred and fifty
one thousand, two hundred and forty-five
one hundred and twenty thousand, four hundred and fifty
items.e: 12 450 is 12 thousands, 4 hundreds and 5 tens: twelve thousand, four hundred and fifty.

items.q: Mia’s step goal is 10 000 steps a day. The arrow shows how many steps she has walked so far. About how many steps is that?
items.e: Each mark is 1000 steps. The arrow is halfway between 6000 and 7000, so it shows about 6500 steps.

items.q: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 7, 2 and 9 once to make the greatest 5-digit number.
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the ten thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 7, 4, 2, 0. The greatest number is 97 420.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 0, 8 and 5 once to make the smallest 4-digit number.
items.e: A 4-digit number cannot start with 0, so put the smallest non-zero digit first: 3. Then 0, 5, 8. The smallest number is 3058.

items.q: There are 10 000 people at the cricket. Then 1000 more people arrive. How many people are there now?
items.e: 1000 more changes only the thousands digit: 0 thousands → 1 thousand. 10 000 + 1000 = 11 000.

items.q: Harper’s number has 4 ten thousands, 2 thousands, 0 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones. What is her number?
items.e: Write the digits in order: 4, 2, 0, 6, 0 → 42 060. The zeros keep the other digits in their places.

items.q: A farm has 2307 sheep. Grace says the 3 is worth 3. What is the 3 really worth?
items.e: In 2307 the 3 is in the hundreds place. Its value is 3 hundreds = 300.

items.q: Footy tickets are printed in packs of 1000. How many packs are needed for 25 000 tickets?
items.e: 25 000 = 25 thousands, because 25 × 1000 = 25 000. So 25 packs are needed.

items.q: Three country towns have populations of 14 205, 14 520, 14 052. Which list shows them from largest to smallest?
items.e: All have 14 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 5 hundreds > 2 hundreds > 0 hundreds. Order: 14 520, 14 205, 14 052.

items.q: The school canteen sold 1098 icy poles last term and 1089 this term. Which is true?
items.e: Both have 1 thousand and 0 hundreds. Compare the tens: 9 tens > 8 tens. So 1098 > 1089.

items.q: A class collects bottle tops. They have 3 bags of 1000, 14 bags of 100 and 5 single bottle tops. How many bottle tops is that?
items.e: 14 hundreds = 1 thousand and 4 hundreds. So there are 4 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones: 3000 + 1400 + 5 = 4405.
